## Paper

Optimal auctions through deep learning

## World

auction_house

## Institution

Learned auction design / RegretNet-style mechanism learning.

## Agent type

Neural mechanism designer and strategic bidders in prior work; bidder learners in this repo.

## Theoretical benchmark

Revenue maximization subject to incentive compatibility/regret and individual-rationality constraints.

## Learning setup

Differentiable mechanism learning in the paper; repeated learned bidder behavior in this repo.

## Metrics

Revenue, regret/IC violation, allocative efficiency, bidder surplus, generalization.

## Main result

The paper demonstrates that deep learning can be used to design optimal auctions that achieve low regret and high revenue, closely matching known optimal solutions and finding novel mechanisms for previously unsolved settings.

## What they prove

Generalization bounds for neural network-based auction designs; regret minimization guarantees; empirical results showing near-optimal auctions for known settings and novel mechanisms for unknown settings.

## What they only simulate

Empirical results on regret, revenue, and efficiency without formal proofs for all settings; simulation of auction outcomes based on neural network predictions.

## What they do NOT test

The paper does not test the robustness of the approach to adversarial valuations or provide formal guarantees for all possible auction settings.

## What we need to reproduce

Auction House must include regret or incentive-compatibility proxies, revenue, allocative efficiency, and truthful/strategic benchmarks.

## How our project differs

The paper learns mechanisms. This repo currently learns bidder behavior under fixed mechanisms, so it can borrow the metric discipline but not claim mechanism-learning equivalence.

## Implementation obligations

Ex-post regret; revenue; allocative efficiency; benchmark bid curves; future exploitability under learned misreports if mechanism learning is added.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

Auction House regret, revenue, efficiency, over/underbidding diagnostics; outputs/auction_house_full; variant smoke outputs.

## Failure modes to audit

Evaluating auctions only by bidder reward; omitting IC/regret; claiming RegretNet-style contribution without learning the mechanism; no generalization check.

## Project code comparison

Compare Optimal auctions through deep learning to worlds/auction_house/benchmarks.py and Auction House outputs. The repo should cite it as a metric obligation for auction learning, while stating that mechanisms are fixed rather than learned.
